title: Self-Supervised and Contrastive Learning
overview: Self-supervised learning builds training signals from the data itself, so large unlabeled datasets can teach useful representations. Contrastive methods pull together views of the same example and push apart others.
objectives: Explain pretext tasks and why they need no labels
Compute an InfoNCE style contrastive loss

method.title: Pretext tasks
method.body: Masked prediction, next-token prediction and augmentation matching create supervision without human labels.

method.title: Contrastive loss
method.body: Two augmented views of one image form a positive pair; other images in the batch act as negatives.

method.title: InfoNCE
method.body: A softmax over similarities encourages the positive pair to score higher than all negatives, usually with a temperature.

method.title: Evaluation
method.body: Freeze the encoder and train a linear classifier (linear probe) to measure representation quality.

pseudocode:
za, zb = normalize(f(aug1(x))), normalize(f(aug2(x)))
sim = za @ zb.T / tau
loss = cross_entropy(sim, arange(B))

playground.starterCode:
import numpy as np
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
za = rng.normal(size=(4, 8)); zb = za + 0.1 * rng.normal(size=(4, 8))  # second view
za /= np.linalg.norm(za, axis=1, keepdims=True)
zb /= np.linalg.norm(zb, axis=1, keepdims=True)
sim = za @ zb.T / 0.1
logp = sim - np.log(np.exp(sim).sum(1, keepdims=True))
loss = -np.mean(np.diag(logp))
print("positive pair similarity:", np.round(np.diag(za @ zb.T), 2))
print("InfoNCE loss:", round(float(loss), 4))

quiz.question: In contrastive learning, a positive pair is:
options: Two views of the same example
